Modifications: retain attested 3–11-letter Russian headwords in lexical POS
(excluding proper names), English glosses, usage labels and form/alternative
relationships with historical wordfreq spelling Zipf >=2.5. Omit media, examples,
quotations, etymology, translations, categories and other enrichment. Tiles use
NFC and uppercase. Й and Ё are distinct from И and Е; no diacritic stripping,
transliteration, Latin lookalikes, stress marks, hyphens or spaces are accepted.
Canonical source spelling is retained separately. Up to eight source entries
and eight senses per entry are bundled for each accepted guess.
Broad guesses include attested inflections, alternative spellings and labelled
regional, historical or sensitive senses. An Е alternative is a separate guess,
not an alias for Ё. Answers require a standalone eligible sense, Zipf >=4.3 and
explicit independent model editorial approval. Selection targets contemporary
standard Russian in Russia, not exhaustive regional separation.

Frequency: wordfreq 3.0.2, Robyn Speer and contributors, revision
372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b, small_ru.msgpack.gz.
https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq/tree/372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b
SHA-256: ddb45281a609f8c5c4bf3ece7b045c540f76fe36bb438a108e2a45c6f593a078
Data: CC BY-SA 4.0. Software: MIT. Complete pinned README and MIT notice supplied.
Preserve all README source credits including OpenSubtitles and freely available
SUBTLEX, Marc Brysbaert and coauthors. No corpus sentences are redistributed.
For case-normalized spellings retain the maximum estimate, not a sum.
For lexical Ё words, frequency uses the maximum exact spelling and Е counterpart
estimate, reflecting ordinary print without dots. This frequency-only fallback
never merges lexical/gameplay keys and may overestimate an individual sense.
Й and И never fold.
Historical mixed-region spelling frequency does not prove current Russian
commonness or sense frequency. No native-human review is claimed.

Sources, pins, policy and reproduction: docs/russian-sources.md and
src/data/russian/source.json in https://github.com/intrepion/kata-inspired-by-wordle-codex-dot

redistributing adapted data. These notices impose no extra restrictions.
